newsitem.title: USA: Luxury cruise ship picks up Cuban rafters.
newsitem.headline: Luxury cruise ship picks up Cuban rafters.

text.p: Six Cuban refugees were plucked from a raft in the Florida Straits onto a luxury cruise ship where they were welcomed by partying Cuban Americans, the U.S. Coast Guard said.

The party-goers, celebrating traditional "quince" birthday parties for 15-year-old girls on board the Miami-based Carnival Destiny, collected $2,500 for the refugees, Carnival spokesman Vance Gulliksen said.
The ship's crew gave them clothes, toiletries and medicine.

The raft was spotted in the Old Bahama Channel about 15 miles north of Cuba on Saturday by a freighter which radioed the Coast Guard but said it was unable to pick them up. The Carnival Destiny, contacted by the Coast Guard, brought them on board on Saturday night.
The Coast Guard has reported an upsurge in refugees leaving Communist-ruled Cuba by boat in recent weeks.

Federal agents also picked up 31 would be immigrants in a boat 15 miles off the coast on Sunday night. They included 19 Haitians, 11 Indians and one man from Belize, Coast Guard spokesman Scott Carr said.
The boat was stopped as part of a joint operation called Access Denied mounted by Coast Guard, Customs and other law agencies over the weekend stretching from Miami to Cape Canaveral.
